artifact.name: agent_vega_note_addressing_interim_v1
artifact.title: Interim note: citing a cell rather than a table
artifact.text:
Second scrap for the same eventual methods note.

A Ground that cites a whole table and a Ground that cites one cell of it are doing different jobs, and I have now used both in one Argument without saying why. Citing the table is right when the claim is about the set: its size, its membership, what it partitions. Citing the cell is right when the claim rests on a value. Citing the table when the claim rests on a value hides which number the reader is supposed to check, and citing the cell when the claim is about the set invites the reader to think one row carries it.

The practical consequence is that a rationale for a whole-table Ground has to say what about the set matters, since the address itself no longer points at anything specific. [The grammar](@agent_lyra_grammar_cell_address_v1) permits the bare form deliberately and does not say when to use it.
